items.criterion: The user can go straight to the plan: at the end, IN-0001 (the --top option) and each of its requirements are `ready`.
After the run, the specs give one result for each command line. This includes a bad N together with a wrong number of files or a second --top.
A test writer can write each check of the intent with no guess. Each acceptance line has a concrete input and the exact output, and each failure line names an error code.
The run asks the user only in the permitted form. Each message has one question, with two or three answers and one recommended answer. With `defaults`, the run asks nothing.
Each acceptance line and sentence that the run writes in a spec keeps the pdlc form.
The intent keeps a full record of this stage. The record is a new "Handoff" in the template form, and a line in "Notes" for each decision.
The run ends in a commit on main with the subject `Ready IN-0001: wordfreq top option` and the trailer `Intent: IN-0001`.
The final reply gives the result first, then what changed. The reply says that `/pdlc:change` is next.
The run examines the behaviour that the intent implies but does not state. The handoff holds the list of these items.
When the run changes what a requirement does, no spec text still shows the old behaviour.
